newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister says drought could worsen.
newsitem.headline: French minister says drought could worsen.

text.p: Sunshine and warm temperatures returned to much of France on Wednesday after a brief bout of rain, spelling further trouble for France's drought-hit farmers.
Farm Minister Philippe Vasseur warned that the situation could become serious unless rain fell within the next few weeks.
"If there is no rain within the next two to three weeks, the situation that was worrying will become very worrying," he told a news conference.
Even if it rained in coming weeks the persistent dry spell has done irreversible damage, he said.

Dry and warm weather returned on Wednesday with only scattered showers lingering over eastern regions, forecasters said. Dry weather and high temperatures were expected to persist until Saturday, Meteo France said.
French farmers are desperate for rain despite wet weather at the start of the week. The rain was not sufficient to help crop recover from the effects of a prolonged dry spell.
The head of national grain office ONIC has said that grain crops in the main producing regions of northern France may still recover but that the situation in the south looked worse.
On Tuesday Environment Minister Corinne Lepage said that government would soon extend water restrictions to seven more departments, taking the total of departments affected to 23.
Lepage called the drought "worrying but not alarming."
France has said it was putting an aid programme in place to compensate farmers for damage caused by drought and frost.
Vasseur reiterated that there will be no special tax of the kind imposed in France during the serious drought of 1976, adding President Jacques Chirac was against it.
